tasks.title: Add one generic atomic plan-revision primitive to M1
tasks.objective: Add apply_plan_revision(repository, old, new, guard, *, config=None, clock=time) -> RevisionApplication to bt_scheduler_core/rebase.py and export it with RevisionGuard, RevisionApplication, accepted_map_digest(state) and stop_generation(state) from bt_scheduler_core. This is the only M1 change of REQ-029 and it is generic: M1 learns no recovery case, diagnosis, proposal, convergence strategy, supplementary audit, grant or conflict bootstrap; those live in T4b/T4c methodology modules that call this primitive through bt_scheduler_adapter. RevisionGuard is a frozen dataclass: operation_key (1-128 printable ASCII), source_sha256, target_sha256, accepted_map_digest, stop_generation (int >= 0), scope (tuple of task ids the revision is declared to change), base_digest (opaque string), current_base (optional zero-argument callable returning the caller's current base digest, evaluated inside the transaction) and barrier_deadline (epoch seconds). accepted_map_digest is sha256 of the canonical JSON {task_id: last attempt id} over COMPLETED tasks whose last attempt is ACCEPTED; stop_generation reads counters['stop'] (0 when absent). Decision order inside one repository transaction, first match wins: (1) no run -> refused no_run; (2) operation_key already in state.revision_applications: same source and target -> outcome adopted with the recorded report and no write, otherwise refused key_conflict; (3) run identity differs from old, old.sha256 != source_sha256, new.sha256 != target_sha256, other plan_id or revision not later -> refused stale_source; (4) paused, cancel_requested or stop_generation(state) != guard.stop_generation -> refused stopped; (5) accepted_map_digest differs -> refused stale_accepted_map; current_base given and its value differs from base_digest or it raises -> refused stale_base; (6) changed = tasks added, removed, or whose preserving fingerprint (ordinary fingerprint plus expected_paths and shared_resources) differs; changed not a subset of scope, or scope names a task in neither plan -> refused out_of_scope; (7) any live attempt -> store state.revision_barrier {operation_key, source, target, deadline} once (deadline later than now + Config.max_recovery_wait -> refused invalid_guard), audit revision_barrier, return waiting with the live attempt ids; reservation._refusal returns revision_pending for every new claim while a barrier whose deadline has not passed exists, never cancelling or pre-empting live attempts; an expired barrier no longer blocks claims and the next call with its key clears it and returns refused barrier_expired; (8) otherwise apply: impacted = scope plus descendants of scope in old and new DAG plus changed; removed tasks are dropped as in rebase_run (attempt history kept, their pending outbox items voided); added tasks start PENDING; impacted existing tasks return to PENDING keeping attempts, budget_base, waits, reworks and hold_until, with reason and route cleared; every other task keeps its record unchanged, so unrelated accepted work stays COMPLETED; set revision and sha, routing_complete False, store revision_applications[key] = {source, target, report, at} (newest 200 kept), clear the barrier, audit task_transition per reset task and one revision_applied {key, from_rev, to_rev, kept, reset, added, removed}, then promote_ready. A refusal writes nothing except clearing that key's own barrier. Observed fact: claim admits a READY task without checking remaining budget and recovery.apply_recovery blocks after a failure once the preserved budget is spent, so a reset exhausted task gets exactly one more attempt. operations.pause and operations.cancel increment counters['stop']. model.py raises STATE_SCHEMA to 3 additively with revision_barrier (None) and revision_applications ({}), reads schema 1 and 2 with those defaults and validates their types. rebase_run, plan_rebase and fingerprint keep their exact current semantics. recovery.py is unchanged (attempt-level retry/wait/block advice, unrelated to diagnostic recovery) and no diagnostic_recovery.py is created.
